text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert PD-84721 fired for service=redwood-infer/runtime-canary - alert=failing_kv_cache_ops. Trigger: deploy-v3.7.1-canary -> 5xx surge + KV cache miss storms
PagerDuty: Paging Jordan (oncall) and ops rotation - escalate in 2m if no ack
Jordan (oncall): Acked. I'm on it. Checking canary cluster metrics now.
Jordan (oncall): Quick summary from Grafana: canary-ns/pod-gen-3 has 3x 500s on /v1/generate and tail latency spike to 3.2s. KV backend errors (redis) show increased EHOSTUNREACH during sustained batching.
Maya: @Jordan any customer reports? Tilly from product pinged CS.
Jordan (oncall): CS says two customers reported timeouts for streaming endpoints ~ 11:02-11:06 UTC (retries still failing). No broad outage yet but error rate > 5% on canary.
Lee: Looking at deploy logs: the model-serving container introduced a change to KV key prefixing in commit d4f2b9 which may be hitting a path in memstore that isn't warmed.
Chao: Reproduced locally with small repro: running canary image + synthetic load -> get rapid connection churn to redis pool after ~150 concurrent streams. Past guardrails didn't trip.
Jordan (oncall): Ok, mitigation plan: 1) pause canary traffic (route away), 2) toggle feature flag to use fallback in-memory cache, 3) if that fails -> rollback canary to previous image.
Jordan (oncall): Pausing canary traffic now: ops-bot: run traffic-router set-weight --service runtime-canary --weight 0 --reason "KV error surge"
ops-bot: command accepted. Routed 100% traffic off canary -> preprod/primary pool.
Maya: Feature-flag toggle ready. Maya: ffctl set runtime.kv_fallback enabled --env canary --who maya
ops-bot: Feature flag runtime.kv_fallback set to enabled for canary (propagation ~10s).
Lee: Watching metrics... KV errors dropping quickly. 500s on /v1/generate falling to baseline. Latency back around 220ms.
Tilly (product): Notifying CS: escalation note to customers that we've routed traffic and applying fallback. No rollback yet.
Chao: Still seeing some residual errors for multi-chunk streams, but nothing at previous scale. Might be a sticky client connection issue.
Jordan (oncall): Rolling back canary image to v3.7.0 as precaution. Command: kubectl -n canary rollout undo deployment/model-serving --to-revision=3 && kubectl -n canary rollout status deployment/model-serving -w
ops-bot: kubectl rollout undo issued, deployment stabilizing.
PagerDuty: Incident PD-84721 acknowledged by Jordan (oncall).
Jordan (oncall): Handing off monitoring to Maya for the next 60m while I finish the post-incident checklist. Maya, you have the incident until 12:20 UTC.
Maya: Ack handoff. I'll monitor dashboard and keep CS updated.
Maya: Confirmed rollback complete, pod restarts healthy. Telemetry looks stable across canary and primary pools.
Tilly (product): Customer impact: two customers experienced transient timeouts, no data loss. Logging correlation IDs: cid-9a3f5 and cid-8b2a1. We'll send a short postmortem note.
Jordan (oncall): Filing immediate notes: suspected root cause = regression in KV key handling + insufficient connection backoff under high concurrent streaming. Follow-ups: add e2e canary test for KV prefixing, enforce redis pool backoff, add canary threshold enforcement for 5xx spike at 1% within 1m.
Chao: I'll open PRs for tests and backoff change. ETA ~ today for tests, backoff next sprint.
Maya: Marking incident as mitigated. PD-84721 -> status: resolved (monitoring for 30m).
incident-bot: Incident PD-84721 mitigation logged. Notes: traffic routed off canary, fallback cache toggled, canary rolled back to v3.7.0.
Jordan (oncall): Thanks everyone. Quick retrospective sync at 14:00 UTC for rollout process improvements. :thumbsup:
